'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[War in Afghanistan (2001–2021)|War in Afghanistan]]
**[[Taliban insurgency]]
***[[2021 Taliban offensive]]
****[[Fall of Kabul (2021)|Fall of Kabul]]
*****The [[Taliban]] enters [[Kabul]] and seizes the [[Arg (Kabul)|presidential palace]], overthrowing the government. [https://news.sky.com/story/afghanistan-taliban-seize-jalalabad-without-a-fight-kabul-is-now-the-only-big-city-that-it-does-not-control-12382021 (Sky News)] [https://www.washingtonpost.com/world/2021/08/15/afghanistan-taliban-kabul-embassy-jalalabad/ (''The Washington Post'')]
*****[[President of Afghanistan|President]] [[Ashraf Ghani]] agrees to form a team for negotiations and also agrees to step down and allow an interim Taliban government to govern the country amid the insurgent group's advance. Among the people in the negotiation team is the first president of Afghanistan after the 2001 [[United States invasion of Afghanistan|U.S. invasion]], [[Hamid Karzai]]. [https://tolonews.com/afghanistan-174232 (TOLO)]
*****President Ashraf Ghani and [[Vice President of Afghanistan|Vice President]] [[Amrullah Saleh]] leave the country and are currently in [[Tajikistan]]. [https://www.bbc.com/news/live/world-asia-58219963 (BBC News)]
*****Taliban officials indicate that there will be no "transitional government" in Afghanistan, saying that the group expects a complete transfer of power from the Ghani [[Government of Afghanistan|government]]. [https://www.reuters.com/world/asia-pacific/taliban-officials-there-will-be-no-transitional-government-afghanistan-2021-08-15/?taid=61193559eb33530001736ec7 (Reuters)]
*****Secretary-General of the [[United Nations]] [[António Guterres]] calls on the Taliban to exercise restraint and respect human rights, especially those concerning women and girls. Guterres also expressed concern at the civilian casualties in areas of conflict. [https://www.reuters.com/world/un-chief-urges-taliban-restraint-is-concerned-about-women-girls-2021-08-15/ (Reuters)]
*****In his first public comments since going into [[exile]], ousted president [[Ashraf Ghani]] concedes that the Taliban has "won the war" in Afghanistan, saying that "they are now facing a new historical test. Either they will preserve the name and honour of Afghanistan or they will give priority to other places and networks". [https://www.thehindu.com/news/international/afghanistan-president-ashraf-ghani-leaves-country-say-officials/article35927207.ece (''The Hindu'')]
****The Taliban captures [[Jalalabad]], the [[Provinces of Afghanistan|provincial]] capital of the [[Nangarhar Province]]. The [[Jihadism|jihadist]] group faced no resistance as the [[Afghan National Army|Afghan military]] and provincial governor surrendered. Taliban forces also enter the [[Char Asiab District]] of the [[Kabul Province]], advancing within {{convert|11|km}} of Kabul. [https://www.reuters.com/world/asia-pacific/us-troops-arrive-afghan-capital-assist-evacuations-2021-08-14/ (Reuters)] [https://news.sky.com/story/afghanistan-taliban-seize-jalalabad-without-a-fight-kabul-is-now-the-only-big-city-that-it-does-not-control-12382021 (Sky News)] [https://www.independent.co.uk/asia/south-asia/afghanistan-taliban-kabul-ashraf-ghani-b1902651.html (''The Independent'')]
****The Afghan military transfers control of [[Bagram Airfield]], formerly the largest [[United States|U.S.]] [[airbase]] in the country, to the Taliban. Five thousand [[unlawful combatant]]s are freed from the airbase's [[Parwan Detention Facility|military prison]]. [https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/news/defence/afghan-forces-surrender-bagram-air-base-to-taliban/articleshow/85347683.cms (''The Economic Times'')]
****Embassies of [[Western countries]] are evacuated and relocated at Kabul's [[Hamid Karzai International Airport]]. The Russian embassy is not evacuated, as it considers that "the situation in Kabul is a bit tense, but there is no war in the city". The Turkish embassy also remains open. [https://www.theguardian.com/world/live/2021/aug/15/afghanistan-taliban-close-in-on-kabul-as-last-government-stronghold-in-north-falls (''The Guardian'')] [https://www.ft.com/content/12dc9ad8-cd90-4378-86f6-64f70f4062eb (''Financial Times'')]
***[[Withdrawal of United States troops from Afghanistan (2020–2021)|Withdrawal of United States troops from Afghanistan]]
****[[Spokesperson for the United States Department of State|U.S. Department of State spokesperson]] [[Ned Price]] announces that the [[Embassy of the United States, Kabul|U.S. Embassy]] is successfully evacuated. [https://www.cbsnews.com/live-updates/taliban-afghanistan-american-evaucations-live-updates-today-2021-08-15/ (CBS News)]
***Taliban spokesperson Mohammad Naeem says on [[Al Jazeera Media Network|Al Jazeera]] [[Al Jazeera Mubasher|Mubasher]] that the war in Afghanistan is over. [https://www.reuters.com/world/asia-pacific/taliban-spokesman-says-war-is-over-afghanistan-al-jazeera-2021-08-15/ (Reuters)] [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2021/8/16/taliban-says-afghanistan-war-over-as-president-diplomats-flee/ (Al Jazeera)]

'''Disasters and accidents'''
*[[2021 Algeria wildfires]]
**The death toll from the [[wildfire]]s in [[Algeria]] rise to 90 people, including 57 civilians and 33 soldiers. [https://www.africanews.com/2021/08/15/algerian-wildfires-still-raging-death-toll-hits-90-including-33-soldiers/ (Africa News)]
*Heavy rain in [[Japan]] causes a [[landslide]] in [[Okaya, Nagano|Okaya]], [[Nagano Prefecture|Nagano]]. Three people are dead after the landslide damaged their house. [https://www.japantimes.co.jp/news/2021/08/15/national/japan-rain-floods-kyushu/ (''The Japan Times'')]
*A passenger bus overturns on the [[M7 motorway (Hungary)|M7 motorway]], west of [[Budapest]], [[Hungary]], killing eight people and injuring dozens of other passengers. [https://www.reuters.com/world/europe/eight-people-killed-dozens-injured-hungary-bus-crash-police-2021-08-15/ (Reuters)]

'''Health and environment'''
*[[COVID-19 pandemic]]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Asia]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Iran]]
****[[Iran]] reports a record 620 deaths from [[COVID-19]] in the past 24 hours, thereby bringing the nationwide death toll to 97,828. [https://www.france24.com/en/live-news/20210815-iran-s-daily-covid-deaths-top-600-in-new-high (France 24)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Laos]]
****[[Laos]] surpasses 10,000 cases of COVID-19. [http://www.xinhuanet.com/english/asiapacific/2021-08/15/c_1310128540.htm (Xinhua News Agency)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in the Philippines]]
****The [[Philippines]] reports its first case of the [[SARS-CoV-2 Lambda variant]] in a 35-year-old female who is [[asymptomatic]] and recovered after [[Quarantine|isolating]] for 10 days. [https://www.rappler.com/nation/philippines-first-case-covid-19-lambda-variant-august-15-2021 (Rappler)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Thailand]]
****[[Thailand]] surpasses 900,000 cases of COVID-19. [https://www.thestar.com.my/aseanplus/aseanplus-news/2021/08/16/thailand039s-total-covid-19-caseload-tops-900000-as-21882-new-cases-are-confirmed-on-sunday-aug-15 (''The Star'')]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Australia]], [[COVID-19 vaccination in Australia]]
***A batch of the [[Pfizer-BioNTech COVID-19 vaccine]] arrived in [[Australia]] from [[Poland]], in which half of vaccine doses will target people aged 20 to 39 years old in 12 [[Local government areas of New South Wales|local government area]]s of concern across [[New South Wales]]. [https://amp.sbs.com.au/eds/news/article/one-million-pfizer-doses-have-arrived-in-australia-from-poland/e697e070-0fc8-4f11-a33b-bf121ca7a372 (SBS World News)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Serbia]]
***The [[Serbia]]n [[Medicines and Medical Devices Agency of Serbia|health authorities]] authorise a third dose of the [[COVID-19 vaccine]] for [[immunocompromise]]d people, health workers and anyone who was vaccinated at least six months ago, and would begin administering these doses on Tuesday. [https://www.reuters.com/world/europe/serbia-authorises-third-shot-covid-19-vaccine-minister-says-2021-08-15/ (Reuters)]
*[[Singapore]] announces the first [[giant panda]] cub in the city-state when the 12-year-old panda Jia Jia gave birth to a cub at [[River Safari]] after being artificially inseminated with frozen semen from 13-year-old Kai Kai. [https://www.straitstimes.com/singapore/singapore-gets-first-panda-cub-born-to-kai-kai-and-jia-jia-at-river-safari (''The Straits Times'')] [https://amp.rfi.fr/en/singapore-zoo-breeds-first-panda-cub (Radio France Internationale)]

'''International relations'''
*[[Israel–Poland relations]]
**[[Israel]] recalls a top diplomat from [[Poland]], after the country passed a law limiting [[Property restitution in Poland|property restitution]] for Jewish [[Holocaust survivors]]. [https://www.politico.eu/article/israel-diplomat-poland-anti-semitic-unethical-restitution-law/ (''Politico Europe'')]

'''Law and crime'''
*[[2020 Hong Kong national security law|Hong Kong national security law]]
**The [[Civil Human Rights Front]] in [[Hong Kong]] disbands. The pro-democracy group had been under pressure from the government for allegedly being internationally funded. The group's leader [[Figo Chan]] and prominent member [[Jimmy Sham]] are both in prison. [https://www.dw.com/en/hong-kongs-pro-democracy-protest-group-chrf-disbands/a-58869104 (Deutsche Welle)]
*Konstantin Pavlov, the pro-[[Russia]]n mayor of [[Kryvyi Rih]], [[Ukraine]], is found dead at his home with a gunshot wound. The [[National Police of Ukraine]] say that they are currently establishing the circumstances of the mayor's death and have also opened a criminal case. [https://www.reuters.com/world/europe/opposition-mayor-ukrainian-city-found-dead-2021-08-15/ (Reuters)]

'''Politics and elections'''
*[[2021 Canadian federal election]]
**Prime Minister [[Justin Trudeau]] obtains the dissolution of the House of Commons for an election scheduled on September 20. [https://www.cbc.ca/news/politics/federal-election-call-1.6141189 (CBC News)]
*[[2020–21 Malaysian political crisis]]
**Reports emerge of the imminent resignation of [[Prime Minister of Malaysia]] [[Muhyiddin Yassin]] on August 16. [https://www.reuters.com/world/asia-pacific/malaysia-pm-muhyiddin-resign-monday-report-2021-08-15/ (Reuters)]

'''Science and technology'''
*[[Spain]] records the highest temperature ever of 47.4°C (117.3°F) in [[Montoro]], [[Province of Córdoba (Spain)|province of Córdoba]] amid an historic heat wave. [https://www.bignewsnetwork.com/news/270730570/spain-reports-record-breaking-temperature-in-southern-town (Big News Network)]
